sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报 DealBook 负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上对部分采访进行直播，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the White House is blaming the government of Syria for the deadliest chemical weapons attack in years.
sentences.zh: 今天，白宫将近年来最致命的化武袭击归咎于叙利亚政府。

sentences.en: But will that change President Trump's calculus that Syrian President Bashar al-Assad may be a better ally than he is an enemy?
sentences.zh: 但这会改变特朗普总统的算盘吗？他认为叙利亚总统巴沙尔·阿萨德可能是一个比敌人更好的盟友？

sentences.en: And Trump is not on the ballot in the small town of Bolingbroke, Illinois, but he might as well be.
sentences.zh: 而且特朗普并没有在伊利诺伊州的小镇博林布罗克参选，但他给人的感觉就像参选了一样。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月5日，星期三。

sentences.en: Anne, thank you for coming on.
sentences.zh: 安妮，谢谢你接受采访。

sentences.en: I know it's late there.
sentences.zh: 我知道那里已经很晚了。

sentences.en: It's been a long day.
sentences.zh: 这真是漫长的一天。

sentences.en: Anne Bernard is a reporter based in Beirut.
sentences.zh: 安妮·伯纳德是一名常驻贝鲁特的记者。

sentences.en: I called her last night.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚给她打了电话。

sentences.en: What happened today in Syria?
sentences.zh: 叙利亚今天发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, Tuesday morning, several airstrikes happened in this town of Khan Sheikhoun.
sentences.zh: 所以在周二早上，汗谢洪这个小镇发生了几次空袭。

sentences.en: And people started to rush to the rescue.
sentences.zh: 人们开始蜂拥去救援。

sentences.en: And some of the people in the area, either who were rushing to help, who had been nearby the explosion, started to feel ill.
sentences.zh: 该地区的一些人，无论是赶去帮忙的，还是在爆炸附近的，都开始感到身体不适。

sentences.en: And started to collapse or have trouble breathing or to feel their eyes stinging.
sentences.zh: 并开始瘫倒、呼吸困难或感到眼睛刺痛。

sentences.en: There were children lying in the street.
sentences.zh: 街上躺着许多儿童。

sentences.en: They realized there was a chemical involved.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到其中涉及化学物质。

sentences.en: So they started in almost a haphazard way trying to spray the people down.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始用几乎是杂乱无章的方式试图用水冲洗人们。

sentences.en: They didn't really have the proper equipment and get them to hospitals.
sentences.zh: 他们其实没有合适的设备，也没能把他们送往医院。

sentences.en: That was even more difficult because the main hospital in the area had been bombed just two days before.
sentences.zh: 这甚至更加困难，因为该地区的主要医院在仅仅两天前刚刚遭到轰炸。

sentences.en: So all these people were being scattered to small clinics around the area.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些人被分散到了该地区的小诊所里。

sentences.en: Then one of those was hit by a subsequent airstrike.
sentences.zh: 然后其中一家诊所在随后的空袭中被击中。

sentences.en: Many hospitals aren't able to treat these patients because they've been totally taken out of action and destroyed.
sentences.zh: 许多医院无法治疗这些病人，因为它们已经完全瘫痪并被摧毁了。

sentences.en: We don't know where we're going to send these patients down.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道要把这些病人送到哪里去。

sentences.en: So it was really chaotic.
sentences.zh: 所以现场真的非常混乱。

sentences.en: What makes you think that this was a toxin used in this attack?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你认为这次袭击使用的是毒素？

sentences.en: Well, the dead and those who were sickened don't have any visible signs of injury.
sentences.zh: 嗯，死者和中毒者身上没有任何可见的伤痕。

sentences.en: They're lying there as if they're asleep.
sentences.zh: 他们躺在那里，就像睡着了一样。

sentences.en: And the people that are being treated in the hospital, some of them are foaming at the mouth.
sentences.zh: 而在医院接受治疗的人中，有些人正在口吐白沫。

sentences.en: People were struggling to get their breath.
sentences.zh: 人们挣扎着喘息。

sentences.en: This patient behind me has got pinpoint people.
sentences.zh: 我身后的这位病人有针尖大小的瞳孔。

sentences.en: Some of them have their pupils shrunk to the size of a pencil point.
sentences.zh: 他们中一些人的瞳孔缩小到了铅笔尖大小。

sentences.en: Which I will show you the evidence again and again.
sentences.zh: 我将一次又一次地向你展示证据。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: The world doesn't care and no one is doing anything.
sentences.zh: 世界并不在意，也没有人做任何事情。

sentences.en: Of course, nobody knows exactly what agent was used.
sentences.zh: 当然，没有人确切知道使用的是什么毒剂。

sentences.en: But the symptoms are similar to those from nerve agents.
sentences.zh: 但这些症状与神经毒剂的症状相似。

sentences.en: And they look very similar to the victims in that big attack in 2013.
sentences.zh: 而且它们看起来与2013年那场大袭击中的受害者非常相似。

sentences.en: So do we know who's responsible for this attack?
sentences.zh: 那么我们知道是谁对这次袭击负责吗？

sentences.en: Well, we can't say for certain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不能确切地说。

sentences.en: But the rebels, the insurgents don't have airplanes.
sentences.zh: 但叛军和反政府武装没有飞机。

sentences.en: So the strong indication is that these are airstrikes by the Syrian government.
sentences.zh: 所以强烈的迹象表明，这是叙利亚政府的空袭。

sentences.en: By the government of Assad.
sentences.zh: 是阿萨德政府干的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, so I want to step pretty far back for just a minute.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想把时间线往回推很远，就一会儿。

sentences.en: If we think this was an attack by the government of President Assad, and you've made clear that we don't entirely know that, but it's believed,
sentences.zh: 如果我们认为这是总统阿萨德政府发动的袭击——你也已经明确表示我们并不完全知道，但人们认为是这样——

sentences.en: why would Assad use chemical weapons to attack people inside his own country?
sentences.zh: 为什么阿萨德会使用化学武器来攻击他自己国家内部的人民？

sentences.en: Well, you have to step back pretty far in the Syrian conflict since the beginning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你必须把叙利亚冲突的时间线从一开始就往回推很远。

sentences.en: And when was the beginning?
sentences.zh: 那起点是什么时候？

sentences.en: The protest started in March 2011, right around the time that the Arab Spring or the Arab revolts, as we've heard it called, were taking place around the region.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动始于2011年3月，大约正是阿拉伯之春或我们所听到的阿拉伯起义在整个地区发生的时候。

sentences.en: So people came out in the street.
sentences.zh: 所以人们走上了街头。

sentences.en: Should I tell you how it began?
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你它是怎么开始的吗？

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: I mean, some kids in Daraa, in southern Syria, scrawled some graffiti on the wall suggesting that Assad's turn was next.
sentences.zh: 我是说，叙利亚南部德拉的一些孩子在墙上胡乱涂鸦，暗示该轮到阿萨德了。

sentences.en: He would be the next Arab leader to step down.
sentences.zh: 他将是下一个下台的阿拉伯领导人。

sentences.en: And those kids were arrested and tortured.
sentences.zh: 而那些孩子被捕并受到了酷刑。

sentences.en: And people started to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 人们开始抗议。

sentences.en: And the protests grew.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: And the security forces fired on protesters.
sentences.zh: 安全部队向抗议者开枪。

sentences.en: Anger in Syria on Saturdays.
sentences.zh: 叙利亚周六的愤怒情绪。

sentences.en: Protesters regrouped following a huge crackdown by security forces.
sentences.zh: 在安全部队进行了大规模镇压之后，抗议者重新集结。

sentences.en: And protests grew some more.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动进一步扩大。

sentences.en: And there are reports of at least a dozen more people being shot dead by security forces.
sentences.zh: 有报道称，又有至少十几人被安全部队枪杀。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands and eventually hundreds of thousands of people were arrested.
sentences.zh: 数万人，最终数十万人被捕。

sentences.en: Many of them were only peaceful or political protesters, not accused of any violence.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人只是和平或政治抗议者，并未被指控犯有任何暴力罪行。

sentences.en: And eventually, people took up arms against the government.
sentences.zh: 最终，人们拿起武器对抗政府。

sentences.en: And the escalation just kept happening.
sentences.zh: 局势不断升级。

sentences.en: It seemed incredible at the time that artillery was being used against a neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 当时看来难以置信的是，火炮竟然被用来对付一个社区。

sentences.en: Next thing we knew, helicopters were being used to drop bombs on the Damascus suburbs.
sentences.zh: 接下来的事我们都知道了，直升机被用来在大马士革郊区投掷炸弹。

sentences.en: The capital shelling its own suburbs.
sentences.zh: 首都炮轰自己的郊区。

sentences.en: And you thought this was unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 而你曾认为这是不可想象的。

sentences.en: And then airplanes started to be used.
sentences.zh: 然后飞机开始被投入使用。

sentences.en: Then in 2013...
sentences.zh: 接着在2013年……

sentences.en: CNN has obtained videos that were shown on Thursday to members of the Senate Intelligence Committee.
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）获取了周四向参议院情报委员会成员展示的视频。

sentences.en: There was a huge chemical attack in the suburbs of Damascus.
sentences.zh: 在大马士革郊区发生了一场大规模的化学武器袭击。

sentences.en: They show the victims of a chemical weapons attack.
sentences.zh: 它们展示了化学武器袭击的受害者。

sentences.en: And according to intelligence officials, it is specifically a sarin gas attack.
sentences.zh: 根据情报官员的说法，这具体是一场沙林毒气袭击。

sentences.en: More than 1,000 people, I think the number finally was 1,466 people, were killed in those attacks.
sentences.zh: 超过1000人，我想最终的确切数字是1466人，在这些袭击中丧生。

sentences.en: Some of the images in these videos, in fact, all of the images in these videos, are disturbing.
sentences.zh: 这些视频中的一些画面，事实上，这些视频中的所有画面，都令人不安。

sentences.en: But we are showing them to you because the nation is about to make a very momentous decision.
sentences.zh: 但我们之所以向你们展示它们，是因为这个国家即将做出一个非常重大的决定。

sentences.en: Which the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: government and its allies blamed on Assad.
sentences.zh: 政府及其盟友将此归咎于阿萨德。

sentences.en: His government said they didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 他的政府表示他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: They said the rebels did it to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们称是叛军自己干的。

sentences.en: So, as this has unfolded, we've seen, step by step, a government that appears to be willing to use almost any form of force against its people.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着事态的发展，我们一步步看到一个似乎愿意对本国人民使用几乎任何形式武力的政府。

sentences.en: So, in that context, it doesn't seem so crazy to imagine the use of chemical weapons.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那种背景下，想象化学武器的使用似乎就没那么疯狂了。

sentences.en: And it feels like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 感觉美国

sentences.en: has played a really complicated role in that.
sentences.zh: 在其中扮演了一个非常复杂的角色。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Early in the conflict, almost in an aside, in a public statement,
sentences.zh: 在冲突早期，几乎是在一次公开声明的旁白中，

sentences.en: President Obama said that if the government used chemical weapons against its people, that would be a red line.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统表示，如果政府对其人民使用化学武器，那将是一条红线。

sentences.en: A red line for us is we start seeing a whole bunch of chemical weapons moving around or being utilized.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说的红线是，我们开始看到大量化学武器四处转移或被使用。

sentences.en: That would change my calculus.
sentences.zh: 那将改变我的算盘。

sentences.en: That would change my equation.
sentences.zh: 那将改变我的公式。

sentences.en: And so, when this attack happened in August 2013, and well over 1,000 people were killed by chemical weapons,
sentences.zh: 因此，当2013年8月发生这起袭击事件、有远超1000人死于化学武器时，

sentences.en: Syrians opposed to Assad were expecting that there would be some form of military retaliation against him.
sentences.zh: 反对阿萨德的叙利亚人期望会对他采取某种形式的军事报复。

sentences.en: This attack is an assault on human dignity.
sentences.zh: 这次袭击是对人类尊严的侵犯。

sentences.en: It also presents a serious danger to our national security.
sentences.zh: 它也对我们的国家安全构成了严重威胁。

sentences.en: What exactly did Barack Obama do as president?
sentences.zh: 贝拉克·奥巴马作为总统到底做了什么？

sentences.en: The chairman of the Joint Chiefs has informed me that we are prepared to strike whenever we choose.
sentences.zh: 参谋长联席会议主席已经通知我，我们随时准备在我们选择的时机进行打击。

sentences.en: Well, this is the moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是现在。

sentences.en: And I'm prepared to give that order.
sentences.zh: 我已经准备好下达那个命令了。

sentences.en: That critics of Obama's policy will say led to today.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政策的批评者会说，正是这导致了今天的局面。

sentences.en: But the red line was not enforced.
sentences.zh: 但那条红线并没有被执行。

sentences.en: And the perception is that, therefore, Damascus concluded that they could pretty much do anything they wanted
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，因此，大马士革得出结论，他们几乎可以为所欲为，

sentences.en: and that they could continue to carpet bomb civilians and bomb hospitals and schools and use whatever weapons they wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们可以继续对平民进行地毯式轰炸，轰炸医院和学校，并使用他们想用的任何武器。

sentences.en: What had our new president, Donald Trump, said about this?
sentences.zh: 我们的新总统唐纳德·特朗普对此有何评论？

sentences.en: You know, Assad, chemical weapons, his entire...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，阿萨德，化学武器，他的整个……

sentences.en: You're in Beirut, I should remind people.
sentences.zh: 我应该提醒大家，你身在贝鲁特。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没事。

sentences.en: It's life.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活。

sentences.en: So what I was asking was, what has President Trump before Tuesday said about Assad and his whole approach to this conflict?
sentences.zh: 所以我刚才问的是，在周二之前，特朗普总统对阿萨德及其处理这场冲突的整体方针有何说法？

sentences.en: Well, President Trump, ever since the campaign, has said that we really shouldn't be worrying about President Assad and how he treats his people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特朗普总统自竞选以来一直表示，我们真的不应该担心阿萨德总统以及他如何对待自己的人民。

sentences.en: Our only concern should be ISIS and defeating ISIS.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一的关注点应该是 ISIS 以及击败 ISIS。

sentences.en: I believe we have to get ISIS.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须消灭 ISIS。

sentences.en: The Islamic State group.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰国组织。

sentences.en: Right now, Syria is fighting ISIS.
sentences.zh: 目前，叙利亚正在打击 ISIS。

sentences.en: We have people that want to fight both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们有人希望同时打击这两者。

sentences.en: And he's even suggested that maybe Assad could be an ally against ISIS.
sentences.zh: 他甚至暗示，或许阿萨德可以成为打击 ISIS 的盟友。

sentences.en: Now, even the Obama administration began to back away from the idea of ousting President Assad and focused instead on combating ISIS.
sentences.zh: 现在，就连奥巴马政府也开始从赶走阿萨德总统的想法后退，转而专注于打击 ISIS。

sentences.en: But ISIS is not the people who are in the area where this bomb happened today.
sentences.zh: 但 ISIS 并不是今天发生炸弹袭击的那个地区的人群。

sentences.en: But ISIS is in Syria.
sentences.zh: 但 ISIS 在叙利亚。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: ISIS is in Syria, primarily in eastern areas.
sentences.zh: ISIS 在叙利亚，主要在东部地区。

sentences.en: But this is in a town called Khan Sheikhoun in northwestern Syria.
sentences.zh: 但这里是叙利亚西北部一个名为汗谢洪的小镇。

sentences.en: It's held not by ISIS, but by the insurgents that are fighting President Bashar al-Assad, including Qaeda-linked groups, but also including a lot of other local rebel groups,
sentences.zh: 控制这里的不是 ISIS，而是与巴沙尔·阿萨德总统作战的反政府武装，其中包括与基地组织有关联的团体，但也包括许多其他当地的反叛组织，

sentences.en: some of which have been supported by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 其中一些曾得到美国

sentences.en: and its allies.
sentences.zh: 及其盟友的支持。

sentences.en: Is there any plausible justification here that these are dangerous groups, a threat to Syria, a threat to the United States, to the broader world,
sentences.zh: 这里是否存在任何合理的正当理由，认为这些是危险组织，对叙利亚、对美国、对更广泛的世界构成了威胁，

sentences.en: and that the threat might be justification for the kinds of tactics being used?
sentences.zh: 并且这种威胁可能成为所使用的那些战术的正当理由？

sentences.en: Well, not if you believe in any kind of international humanitarian law or limits on how war is conducted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你信仰任何形式的国际人道主义法或对战争行为的限制，那就没有。

sentences.en: No matter who you're fighting, it's illegal to use chemical weapons.
sentences.zh: 无论你在和谁作战，使用化学武器都是非法的。

sentences.en: And the question that the world is facing now is, in an age when there's such an extreme fear of Islamic terrorism,
sentences.zh: 世界现在面临的问题是，在一个对伊斯兰恐怖主义极度恐惧的时代，

sentences.en: is the world ready to accept almost literally any kind of tactic to defeat those groups?
sentences.zh: 世界是否准备好接受几乎字面意义上的任何战术来击败这些组织？

sentences.en: Or even worse, is it willing to tolerate a leader who fights his own people just using the excuse that he's fighting terrorism?
sentences.zh: 或者更糟糕的是，它是否愿意容忍一个仅仅以打击恐怖主义为借口来攻击自己人民的领导人？

sentences.en: Are we really OK with that?
sentences.zh: 我们真的能接受这一点吗？

sentences.en: And just this past Friday, members of the Trump administration, including the ambassador to the United Nations, Nikki Haley, really emphasized that ousting Assad is not a priority.
sentences.zh: 就在上周五，特朗普政府成员，包括美国驻联合国大使尼基·黑利，着重强调驱逐阿萨德并非优先事项。

sentences.en: U.N.
sentences.zh: 联合国

sentences.en: Ambassador Nikki Haley said today that it is no longer the administration's priority to remove leader Assad from office in Syria.
sentences.zh: 黑莉大使今天表示，让叙利亚领导人阿萨德下台已不再是本届政府的首要任务。

sentences.en: Now, ambassador to the U.N., Nikki Haley, said, quote, our priority is no longer to sit there and focus on getting Assad out.
sentences.zh: 现在，美国常驻联合国代表黑莉表示，原话是，我们的优先事项不再是坐在那里专注于让阿萨德下台。

sentences.en: And that the main goal is to fight the Islamic State, Islamic terrorism, as you've pointed out.
sentences.zh: 正如你所指出的，主要目标是打击伊斯兰国和伊斯兰恐怖主义。

sentences.en: So what is the Trump administration saying now following these attacks?
sentences.zh: 那么，在发生这些袭击之后，特朗普政府现在是怎么说的呢？

sentences.en: Well, they just came out with a statement saying that these attacks are reprehensible, blaming them on Mr. Assad's government.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们刚刚发表了一份声明，称这些袭击是令人发指的，并将其归咎于阿萨德先生的政府。

sentences.en: So it'll be interesting to see how they square that circle, because on the one hand, they've been making clear that
sentences.zh: 所以看看他们将如何自圆其说将会很有趣，因为一方面，他们一直在明确表示

sentences.en: that they are far more comfortable with this government staying in power, even than the Obama administration was,
sentences.zh: 他们对这个政府继续留任要舒服得多，甚至超过了奥巴马政府，

sentences.en: and that they're willing to work with Russia and with Assad, perhaps, to fight ISIS.
sentences.zh: 而且他们愿意与俄罗斯甚至阿萨德合作，也许是为了打击ISIS。

sentences.en: So I don't know where Donald Trump is going to go with this.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道唐纳德·特朗普接下来会怎么做。

sentences.en: Anne, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 安妮，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I know it's late there.
sentences.zh: 我知道那边很晚了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks a lot.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for being interested.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的关注。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于对设计的热爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都会带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，你会把DJ台变成这样一个，呃，

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I think that Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth want to get involved in this election.
sentences.zh: 我认为迪克·德宾和塔米·达克沃斯想卷入这次选举。

sentences.en: Are they trying to punish you?
sentences.zh: 他们是在试图惩罚你吗？

sentences.en: Are they trying to make you accountable?
sentences.zh: 他们是在试图让你承担责任吗？

sentences.en: They're trying to punish somebody that was involved with Trump
sentences.zh: 他们试图惩罚一个参与过特朗普事件的人

sentences.en: and show them that the anti-Trump movement is not going away, and we're going to punish you and show you to the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 并向他们表明反特朗普运动并没有消失，我们要惩罚你，并向全世界展示。

sentences.en: In the small town of Bolingbroke, Illinois, 30 miles outside of Chicago, national politics have intruded on what has long been a sleepy small-town race for mayor.
sentences.zh: 在伊利诺伊州博林布鲁克这个距离芝加哥30英里的小镇上，全国政治已经侵入了长期以来一直是一场平静的小镇市长竞选。

sentences.en: So long that the same man, Roger Clare, has held the office for more than three decades.
sentences.zh: 时间长达三十多年，同一个人罗杰·克莱尔一直担任这个职务。

sentences.en: He's 71 years old.
sentences.zh: 他今年71岁。

sentences.en: He is a native of Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 他是博林布鲁克本地人。

sentences.en: Julie Bosman covers the Midwest for The Times and went to Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·博斯曼为《时报》报道中西部新闻，她去了博林布鲁克。

sentences.en: He's really been kind of an unquestioned political force in Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 在博林布鲁克，他真的算是一个无可置疑的政治力量。

sentences.en: It sounds like he runs and wins every time.
sentences.zh: 听起来他每次参选都能获胜。

sentences.en: He runs and wins, and no one in recent memory has put up even a remotely credible challenge to Mayor Clare.
sentences.zh: 他参选并且获胜，近年来没有人对克莱尔市长发起过哪怕稍微有一点可信度的挑战。

sentences.en: This year is different.
sentences.zh: 今年情况不同了。

sentences.en: I'm not naive, but I was a little surprised at the outburst of interest outside of Bolingbroke over this race.
sentences.zh: 我并不天真，但对于博林布鲁克之外对这场竞选爆发出的关注，我还是有点惊讶。

sentences.en: And then, of course, it settled in.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，这种情绪平息了。

sentences.en: Ah, there are people that want to see me put on a stake and start the fire and rotissarize me for my actions last November, or September, actually.
sentences.zh: 啊，有人想把我架在火上烤，像烤全羊一样把我旋转烧烤，因为我去年11月——实际上是9月——的所作所为。

sentences.en: So, Julie, what happened in September of 2016?
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，2016年9月发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, last September, Donald Trump was the Republican nominee for president, and he came to the Chicago area to raise some money.
sentences.zh: 所以，去年9月，唐纳德·特朗普是共和党总统候选人，他来到芝加哥地区筹集资金。

sentences.en: Now, previous presidential candidates would have big, glitzy fundraisers in downtown Chicago.
sentences.zh: 现在，以前的总统候选人会在芝加哥市中心举办盛大、华丽的筹款活动。

sentences.en: So, it was notable and a little weird that when Trump came here last fall, he went to Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 因此，去年秋天特朗普来到这里时，他去了博林布鲁克，这引人注目且有点奇怪。

sentences.en: I got the call.
sentences.zh: 我接到了电话。

sentences.en: He went to Bolingbroke for an event at the Bolingbroke Golf Club.
sentences.zh: 他去博林布鲁克是为了在博林布鲁克高尔夫俱乐部举办一场活动。

sentences.en: Would the club be able to handle it because the people weren't sure they heard about the golf club?
sentences.zh: 俱乐部能应付得来吗，因为人们不确定他们是否听说过这个高尔夫俱乐部？

sentences.en: Which is the big, lavish golf course that Roger Clare had built.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗杰·克莱尔建造那个大型、豪华高尔夫球场的地方。

sentences.en: So, simply, is it available?
sentences.zh: 所以，简单地说，它有空吗？

sentences.en: I called and said it is, and I said, well, we'd like to come out there.
sentences.zh: 我打电话说有空，我说，我们想去那里。

sentences.en: I said, fine.
sentences.zh: 我说，好的。

sentences.en: What was the reaction to this fundraiser?
sentences.zh: 对这次筹款活动的反应是什么？

sentences.en: So, some people probably thought it was great because there certainly are plenty of Trump supporters in Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人可能觉得这很好，因为博林布鲁克确实有很多特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: But Bolingbroke has really changed over the last few decades since Roger Clare has been in charge.
sentences.zh: 但自从罗杰·克莱尔掌权以来的几十年里，博林布鲁克确实发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: Trump!
sentences.zh: 特朗普！

sentences.en: Trump!
sentences.zh: 特朗普！

sentences.en: Trump!
sentences.zh: 特朗普！

sentences.en: Trump!
sentences.zh: 特朗普！

sentences.en: Trump!
sentences.zh: 特朗普！

sentences.en: This despicable person, this con man, who plays to racists, bigots, and haters.
sentences.zh: 这个卑鄙的人，这个骗子，他迎合种族主义者、盲信者和仇恨者。

sentences.en: Man, I know you, and you're better than this.
sentences.zh: 老兄，我认识你，你比这更好。

sentences.en: You know, when it was first founded back in the 60s, it was probably almost all white.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当它在60年代初首次建立时，可能几乎全是白人。

sentences.en: And now it has a pretty sizable African-American population, Latino population.
sentences.zh: 而现在它拥有相当规模的非裔美国人和拉丁裔人口。

sentences.en: It has two mosques.
sentences.zh: 它有两座清真寺。

sentences.en: There are a lot of Muslims in Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 博林布鲁克有很多穆斯林。

sentences.en: This is a very diverse community out here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常多元化的社区。

sentences.en: And they went to Clare and asked him not to invite Trump out here.
sentences.zh: 他们去找克莱尔，要求他不要邀请特朗普来这里。

sentences.en: We talked to one man, African-American man, who said, I really feel like the mayor wasn't being aware of everybody's feelings when he did this.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了一名男子，一名非裔美国男子，他说，我真的觉得市长在做这件事时没有顾及每个人的感受。

sentences.en: And he just snubbed his nose and invited him anyway.
sentences.zh: 而他只是嗤之以鼻，无论如何还是邀请了他。

sentences.en: The way he talks about minorities, people get insulted by Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他谈论少数族裔的方式，让人们对唐纳德·特朗普感到被侮辱。

sentences.en: And when they realize that, yeah, that was the mayor that brought him here, that definitely turns their head to think, hmm, maybe I ought to look at a few other things.
sentences.zh: 当他们意识到，是的，正是市长把他带到这里的，这绝对让他们转过头去想，嗯，也许我应该看看其他一些事情。

sentences.en: One of the people who was really angry was Jackie Trenier.
sentences.zh: 杰基·特雷尼尔是真正愤怒的人之一。

sentences.en: She is a native of Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 她是博林布鲁克的本地人。

sentences.en: She is a labor organizer.
sentences.zh: 她是一名工会组织者。

sentences.en: And she decided that she was going to run against Roger Clare because she was so angry about the fact that he brought Donald Trump to Bolingbroke.
sentences.zh: 她决定竞选对抗罗杰·克莱尔，因为她对克莱尔把唐纳德·特朗普带到博林布鲁克这一事实感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: So all of a sudden, Mayor Clare has an opponent.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，克莱尔市长有了一个对手。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he really did not see this coming.
sentences.zh: 而他真的没有预料到这一点。

sentences.en: He didn't think this would backfire.
sentences.zh: 他没想到这会产生反效果。

sentences.en: I'm disappointed that some people will take that one thing after 31 years of service and say, that's it.
sentences.zh: 我很失望，有些人会在31年的服务之后抓住那一件事说，就是这样。

sentences.en: So when Jackie decided to run, she very quickly had endorsements from Dick Durbin, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以当杰基决定参选时，她很快就得到了这里的美国参议员迪克·德宾、

sentences.en: senator here, from Tammy Duckworth, powerful Democrats in the state who would normally not be interested in getting involved in a village mayoral election.
sentences.zh: 州内权势巨大的民主党人塔米·达克沃斯的背书，他们通常对参与村长选举不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But here they are, which is very unusual.
sentences.zh: 但他们在这里，这非常罕见。

sentences.en: This village from 53 years has always had nonpartisan races.
sentences.zh: 这个拥有53年历史的村庄一直举行无党派竞选。

sentences.en: People have asked me, why don't you go out and get some Republican endorsements?
sentences.zh: 人们问我，你为什么不去争取一些共和党人的背书？

sentences.en: I said no, because there's no such thing as a Republican or Democratic pothole.
sentences.zh: 我说不，因为根本没有什么共和党或民主党的坑洼。

sentences.en: I don't want some highly elected Republican official in Springfield or Washington calling me, asking me, you owe me, I helped you in your last race.
sentences.zh: 我不希望斯普林菲尔德或华盛顿某个高级民选共和党官员打电话给我，问我，你欠我的，我在你的上一次竞选中帮了你。

sentences.en: You know, he has a point there that this is not an election that was usually about who's a Republican and who's a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他说的有道理，这不是一场通常关于谁是共和党人、谁是民主党人的选举。

sentences.en: I wonder, Julie, if you've met anyone who says that 30 years of governing, you know, shouldn't be tossed aside or forgotten over a single luncheon fundraiser.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，我想知道你是否遇到过这样的人，他们说30年的执政，你知道，不应该因为一次午宴筹款活动就被抛在一边或遗忘。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, there are a ton of people who said, look, Roger has done great things for us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有大量的人说，听着，罗杰为我们做过伟大的事情。

sentences.en: I've always been very proud to say that I live in Bolingbroke and that Roger Clear is a mayor.
sentences.zh: 我一直非常自豪地说我住在博林布鲁克，罗杰·克莱尔是市长。

sentences.en: Terry Wintermute is a volunteer for the mayor's re-election campaign, and I reached her at his headquarters.
sentences.zh: 特里·温特穆特是市长连任竞选的志愿者，我在他的竞选总部联系到了她。

sentences.en: You know, when we started, there wasn't a grocery store in Bolingbroke, but there was one very small one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们开始时，博林布鲁克连一家杂货店都没有，只有一个非常小的杂货店。

sentences.en: But you couldn't buy a pair of shoes in Bolingbroke at that point in time.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，你在博林布鲁克连一双鞋都买不到。

sentences.en: And he brought a ton of businesses.
sentences.zh: 他带来了大量的企业。

sentences.en: He brought retail.
sentences.zh: 他带来了零售业。

sentences.en: He has built bigger and better houses.
sentences.zh: 他建造了更大更好的房屋。

sentences.en: You know, he's encouraged diversity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他鼓励多元化。

sentences.en: Do you think it's fair that he's being judged on that one day over 31 years in office?
sentences.zh: 你认为因为那一天的事而在任职31年后对她进行评判是公平的吗？

sentences.en: Kind of the phrase, don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.
sentences.zh: 有点像那句话，不要把婴儿和洗澡水一起倒掉。

sentences.en: You know, I myself was not a Trump fan, but I can't turn my back on all those fantastic, well-thought-out, planned things that Mayor Claire has done for the village.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我自己也不是特朗普的粉丝，但我不能背弃克莱尔市长为村庄做过的所有那些美妙的、深思熟虑的、有计划的事情。

sentences.en: So I don't see what national politics has to do with this race at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为全国政治与这场竞选根本没有任何关系。

sentences.en: It is going to be a long while until we have our next round of big elections in the United States.
sentences.zh: 距离我们在美国举行下一轮大选还要很长一段时间。

sentences.en: What does this small race in a small town in Illinois tell us, you think, about what elections all over the country might look like with Trump as our president now?
sentences.zh: 你认为伊利诺伊州一个小镇的这场小选举告诉了我们什么，关于在特朗普现在作为我们总统的情况下，全国各地的选举可能会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I think what you have here is a lot of people who just want to make a statement and at least explain in one vote how they feel about the president and his allies.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有很多只是想表明立场的人，并且至少在一张选票中解释他们对总统及其盟友的感受。

sentences.en: There's some things I want to finish.
sentences.zh: 有些事情我想完成。

sentences.en: I enjoy the job.
sentences.zh: 我很享受这份工作。

sentences.en: I've talked to a lot of people retired, and they say, if you don't have a game plan, don't quit.
sentences.zh: 我和许多退休的人谈过，他们说，如果你没有长远计划，就不要辞职。

sentences.en: So I don't have a game plan.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有长远计划。

sentences.en: I don't have any hobbies.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何爱好。

sentences.en: My hobby is government.
sentences.zh: 我的爱好就是政府工作。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the residents of Bolingbroke voted for their next mayor.
sentences.zh: 周二，博林布鲁克的居民投票选出了他们的下一任市长。

sentences.en: It remains extremely close.
sentences.zh: 选情依然极其胶着。

sentences.en: As of this morning, Mayor Roger Claire was up by just about 100 votes out of more than 12,000 ballots caSt.
sentences.zh: 截至今天早上，在投出的12,000多张选票中，罗杰·克莱尔市长仅仅领先大约100票。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: Attorney General Jeff Sessions has ordered a sweeping review of dozens of federal agreements with local police departments designed to improve relations between officers and the communities they serve.
sentences.zh: 司法部长杰夫·塞申斯下令对联邦与地方警察局达成的数十项旨在改善警员与其所服务社区之间关系的协议进行全面审查。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, in recent years, law enforcement as a whole, I think, has been unfairly maligned and blamed for unacceptable deeds of a few bad actors.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，近年来，我认为整个执法部门一直遭到不公正的诋毁，并被归咎于少数害群之马不可接受的行为。

sentences.en: And the NCAA said it would lift its ban on holding major sporting events in North Carolina after the state rolled back a controversial law that required transgender people to use the bathroom that corresponds to the gender on their birth certificate.
sentences.zh: 美国大学体育协会表示，在该州废除了一项要求跨儿使用与其出生证明上的性别相符的卫生间的争议性法律后，它将解除在北卡罗来纳州举办大型体育赛事的禁令。

sentences.en: But the NCAA said it was doing so, quote, reluctantly.
sentences.zh: 但美国大学体育协会表示，它这样做是，引述，“勉强的”。

sentences.en: The repeal did not go far enough for many LGBTQ advocates.
sentences.zh: 对于许多LGBTQ倡导者来说，废除该法还远远不够。

sentences.en: It lifted the ban, but did not allow local anti-discrimination laws to be passed until 2020.
sentences.zh: 它解除了禁令，但在2020年之前不允许通过地方反歧视法。

sentences.en: It continues to say to vibrant cities and towns across the state of North Carolina that they can't protect their most vulnerable LGBT citizens with vital non-discrimination protections for four years.
sentences.zh: 它继续向北卡罗来纳州全州充满活力的城市和小镇表示，他们不能用至关重要的反歧视保护措施来保护其最脆弱的LGBT公民，持续四年之久。

sentences.en: That's a very long time.
sentences.zh: 那是非常长的时间。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》就到这里。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天选举迎来了许多自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在这个过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
